extraction.name: PIQA: Physical Interaction: Question Answering
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning framed as multiple-choice question answering: given a physical goal expressed in natural language, a system must choose the most sensible solution between two options.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi
extraction.publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI)
extraction.citeAs: Bisk, Y., Zellers, R., Le Bras, R., Gao, J., and Choi, Y. 2020. PIQA: Reasoning about Physical Commonsense in Natural Language. In Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from crowd annotators prompted with instructions from instructables.com across six categories (costume, outside, craft, home, food, workshop). Annotators were asked to articulate a physical goal, a valid solution, and an invalid solution (trick) based on the instructable.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was filtered using the AFLite algorithm to systematically reduce annotation artifacts and spurious data biases by discarding instances whose feature representations are collectively highly indicative of the target label. Examples with low agreement during validation were removed, and sequences were truncated at 150 tokens.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were prompted with links to instructables to provide a physical goal, a valid solution, and an invalid trick solution (often via subtle semantic perturbations). Annotators had to pass a qualification HIT (>80% accuracy) and validation HITs were conducted to check correctness and agreement. The interface included a diff button highlighting solution differences.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (implied via HITs and turkerview.com)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Validation HITs evaluated agreement across annotators; examples with low agreement were discarded. Human performance benchmark was calculated using majority vote.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Reporting bias in physical commonsense knowledge (everyday physical properties are rarely directly reported in text); annotator bias towards prototypical solutions (mitigated via instructables prompts); annotation artifacts and stylistic biases (mitigated via AFLite adversarial filtering).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Text is inherently limited for physical domains due to reporting bias; some development errors in evaluation were actually correct but required a web search to verify; correct examples requiring expert-level knowledge were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating physical commonsense understanding in natural language processing models (training, validation, testing).
